        How status is decided

        Each event's last 3 days are compared with the 7 days before. Escalating: severity up at least a point (with 2+ reports) or coverage up 50% or more (with 4+ reports). Cooling: severity down a point or coverage halved. New: first reported in the last 3 days. Quiet: no reports in 3 days.

        Forecasts

        Each week the agent makes specific yes/no forecasts with deadlines. When a deadline passes it checks the news to see what happened, and every forecaster is scored with the Brier score: lower is better, 0 is perfect, and always saying 50% scores 0.25.

        Add your own forecasts

        Open my_forecasts.csv in the GitHub repository, select the pencil icon and add a line with the forecast ID and your probability, for example F261022-1,35%. Add yes or no as a third value to settle an outcome yourself. Your forecasts appear after the next daily run.

        Where the risks are

        Each marker is one distinct event, placed where it is happening. Size and colour show severity, not how often it was reported, so a single grave event stands out more than a minor story covered many times.
